answer: Rhythm-Locked Registration. Each new identity must sustain a randomized inter-arrival interval drawn from a hidden umber distribution for its first 48 hours; arrivals too uniform or too bursty are rejected. The gate holds registration until the agent’s traffic matches a slow tundra of steady heartbeats. Genuine agents tolerate this wait; a sybil farm pays a per-identity delay of hours plus idle compute to fake each vine of plausible timing, making bulk identities linearly expensive in wall-clock time.
